text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri says Egypt is ready for huge investment projects and will provide all guarantees to attract them. A draft investment law will provide incentives and ease procedures. Cabinet and businessmen will discuss prices of fuels like natural gas for industrial projects.
- President Mubarak and President Arafat discuss the latest developments in the Palestinian-Israeli peace talks.
- Egypt to reclaim 1.8 million acres (730,000 hectares) of desert land for agriculture.
- Scientific research ministry to set up office in Red Sea resort town of Hurghada to meet the needs of investors.
- Mubarak, Arafat talks aim at saving peace. Palestinian negotiator says Egypt is the real sponsor of the peace talks.
- Prime minister tells ministers and businessmen: "Confiscation and nationalisation are paths that the government will never take again".
- Pharaonic, Roman and Greek burial site found. Archeologists have dug out sarcophagi, pottery and gold.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says Egypt contacting U.S. President Clinton and holding talks with the EU envoy to find a fair and just solution to the deadlock in peace talks.
